papers.title: Identification of Gene Signatures and Molecular Mechanisms Underlying the Comorbidity of Alzheimer's Disease and Crohn's Disease Using Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Crohn's disease (CD) both involve inflammation and immune dysregulation, yet the potential molecular mechanisms underlying their comorbidity remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify shared gene signatures and molecular mechanisms linking Alzheimer's disease and Crohn's disease, two conditions both characterized by inflammation and immune dysregulation. The authors aim to uncover common pathways that could explain their comorbidity, potentially revealing shared therapeutic targets.

papers.title: The pod components of the Shigella T3SS sorting platform accommodate multiple copies of Spa33 (SctQ).
papers.abstract: The bacterial type III secretion system (T3SS) uses a membrane-embedded injectisome assembly to export effector proteins into host cells. While atomic-level structural details have been revealed for much of the T3SS apparatus, the model of the cytoplasmic sorting platform remains largely low-resolution. A central structural element of the sorting platform is the so-called "pod" protein, SctQ, which anchors the sorting platform to the inner membrane via interaction with the adaptor protein SctK, and connects to the central ATPase via the spoke protein SctL. SctQ proteins also interact with alte
papers.summary: This study investigates the structural organization of the Shigella type III secretion system's cytoplasmic sorting platform, focusing on the 'pod' protein Spa33 (SctQ). The authors find that the pod components can accommodate multiple copies of Spa33, providing new insights into how this low-resolution region of the injectisome is assembled. This advances understanding of the stoichiometry and architecture of a key bacterial virulence apparatus.

papers.title: FuTCM-PDD: a multi-level information fusion framework integrating KAN modeling and AutoML for phenotype-based drug discovery from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.abstract: Phenotype-based drug discovery has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in first-in-class drug development and higher clinical translation rates. Chinese Materia Medica (CMM), with its emphasis on properties and efficacies, provides a unique framework for phenotype-oriented therapeutic discovery. We developed an AI-driven framework, FuTCM-PDD, that integrates CMMs, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, CMM efficacies, and CMM properties to enable phenotype-based drug discovery. For drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) m
papers.summary: FuTCM-PDD is an AI framework that fuses multi-level information—Chinese Materia Medica, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, and traditional efficacy/property descriptors—to support phenotype-based drug discovery. It uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for drug-target interaction prediction combined with AutoML to link traditional medicine knowledge with modern phenotypic screening. The work aims to bridge traditional Chinese medicine theory and computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Odorant receptor structures predict the major female sex pheromone component in a moth.
papers.abstract: Species isolation in insects can be ensured by prezygotic barriers, such as species-specific sex pheromone blends that mediate sexual attraction and mate recognition. Yet, sex pheromone compositions of many species remain poorly characterized outside important agricultural pests, because of the necessity to access live insects for pheromone extraction, the difficulties in identifying the production period, and the precise identification of behaviorally relevant compounds in extracts.
papers.summary: This study uses odorant receptor protein structures to predict the major sex pheromone component produced by female moths, offering a computational shortcut to pheromone identification that avoids the need for live insect sampling and behavioral assays. The approach could accelerate characterization of sex pheromones across many insect species, with implications for pest management and understanding of species isolation.

papers.title: In vitro, in vivo, and computational evaluation of xanthine oxidase inhibitory and antihyperuricemic activities of Piper betle L. ethyl acetate fraction.
papers.abstract: Gout is a metabolic disorder characterized by hyperuricemia and urate crystal deposition. This study evaluated the xanthine oxidase inhibitory, antihyperuricemic, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and in silico target-binding properties of an EtOAc fraction of Piper betle L. aerial parts.
papers.summary: This study evaluates an ethyl acetate fraction of Piper betle (betel leaf) for its ability to inhibit xanthine oxidase and lower uric acid levels, using in vitro assays, in vivo animal models, and computational docking. The fraction showed xanthine oxidase inhibition, antihyperuricemic, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic effects, with in silico analysis suggesting binding to relevant targets. The findings support the traditional use of Piper betle as a potential complementary treatment for gout.

papers.title: Computational prioritization of megalin-aminoglycoside recognition and gentamicin-associated cellular stress responses.
papers.abstract: Aminoglycosides are effective antibiotics for severe infections, but their clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity resulting from drug accumulation in non-infected tissues. Megalin, an endocytic receptor expressed in renal proximal tubules and inner-ear tissues, has been proposed as a mediator of this uptake.
papers.summary: This computational study investigates how the endocytic receptor megalin recognizes aminoglycoside antibiotics like gentamicin, which is thought to drive their accumulation in kidney and inner-ear tissues and cause toxicity. The authors prioritize potential megalin-aminoglycoside binding interactions and downstream cellular stress responses, offering mechanistic hypotheses for aminoglycoside-induced nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based multiclass model that predicts mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability, explicitly encoding reference and mutant sequences together rather than independently. The authors apply it to CcsZ, demonstrating utility for ranking variants in protein engineering workflows where experimental screening is costly.

papers.title: AASIA: A comprehensive protein structural interactome database for agricultural animals.
papers.abstract: Agricultural animals are essential for global food production and sustainable agriculture. Improving disease resistance and economically important traits is critical for ensuring food security. Proteome-wide protein-protein interactions (PPIs), termed as interactomes, underlie key biological processes in cells, making them critical for deciphering the genome-phenome relationship. However, species-specific PPI resources remain limited for most agricultural animals.
papers.summary: AASIA is a new database that compiles proteome-wide protein-protein interaction (interactome) data for agricultural animals, addressing the scarcity of species-specific PPI resources for these organisms. It aims to support research on disease resistance and economically important traits by helping link genomes to phenotypes in livestock and other farmed species.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, in silico studies, and biological evaluation of tosyl-substituted thiazoles, thiazolidin-4-ones, and chromenes as potential anticancer agents.
papers.abstract: A novel series of thiazole, thiazolidin-4-one, and chromene derivatives incorporating a 4-methylbenzenesulfonate (tosylate) moiety were designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their anticancer potential. All structures were elucidated using IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and MS spectroscopy. Anticancer potential was assessed by MTT assay against HepG-2 (hepatocellular carcinoma) and MCF-7 (breast cancer) cell lines, with doxorubicin as a reference. Against MCF-7, compounds 3d (IC50 = 28.2 ± 2.08 µM), 6a (30.0 ± 0.82 µM), and 8a (25.9 ± 1.35 µM) exhibited relatively enhanced cytotoxicity. For HepG-2, de
papers.summary: This paper reports the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of new tosyl-substituted thiazole, thiazolidin-4-one, and chromene compounds as potential anticancer agents. Several derivatives showed moderate cytotoxicity against liver (HepG-2) and breast (MCF-7) cancer cell lines in MTT assays, though with IC50 values in the micromolar range that are weaker than the doxorubicin reference. The work is primarily a medicinal chemistry synthesis and screening study with limited mechanistic or in vivo follow-up.

papers.title: Exploring the potential mechanism of Xiaoqinglong Decoction in the treatment of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease based on network pharmacology and in silico study.
papers.abstract: Xiaoqinglong Decoction (XQLD) is a traditional Chinese herbal formula widely used in clinical practice to treat acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with notable efficacy. Studies indicate that XQLD can effectively modulate the inflammatory response during the acute infectious phase of AECOPD; however, its underlying mechanism of action remains unclear. This study employed network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the potential target genes of XQLD and its possible mechanisms of action in treating AECOPD. Active
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict the targets and mechanisms by which Xiaoqinglong Decoction, a traditional Chinese herbal formula, treats acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The authors identify candidate target genes and propose that the formula modulates inflammatory responses, though findings are computational predictions without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses reveal VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking environmental bisphenol A exposure to MASH-HCC progression.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC) is an increasingly important subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma, and environmental contaminants have been proposed as potential contributors to its progression. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in metabolic dysfunction and liver injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking BPA exposure to MASH-HCC remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed an integrated framework combining transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis,
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with network analysis and experimental validation to identify VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC). The findings suggest that environmental BPA exposure may contribute to liver cancer progression through VIPR1-related molecular pathways.

papers.title: Integrative AI-assisted modeling suggests CPPF binding at a composite [Formula: see text]/[Formula: see text]-tubulin interface pocket dominated by [Formula: see text]-tubulin contacts.
papers.abstract: Microtubules are dynamic cytoskeletal polymers assembled from α/β-tubulin heterodimers. Microtubules are validated targets for novel therapeutic drugs, yet therapeutic efficacy targeting them is often compromised by multidrug resistance (MDR). 5-(3-chlorophenyl)-N-(3-pyridinyl)-2-furamide (CPPF) is a novel microtubule-targeting anticancer agent which was found to disrupt microtubule growth in cells and inhibit tubulin polymerization in vitro. CPPF could suppress the growth of multidrug-resistant cell lines and demonstrate anti-tumor efficacy in animal models. However, the fundamental mechanism
papers.summary: This study uses integrative AI-assisted computational modeling to predict how the novel anticancer compound CPPF binds to tubulin, the building block of microtubules. The models suggest CPPF occupies a composite pocket at the interface between α- and β-tubulin, with binding dominated by contacts to β-tubulin. This provides a structural hypothesis for how CPPF disrupts microtubule polymerization and may help explain its activity against multidrug-resistant cancer cells.

papers.title: Linear antibody epitope prediction using AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: Defining the binding epitopes of antibodies is essential for understanding how they bind to their antigens and perform their molecular functions. However, while determining linear epitopes of monoclonal antibodies can be accomplished utilizing well-established empirical procedures, these approaches are generally labor- and time-intensive, and costly. To take advantage of the recent advances in protein structure prediction algorithms available to the scientific community, we developed a calculation pipeline based on the localColabFold implementation of AlphaFold2 that can predict linear antibod
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational pipeline using AlphaFold2 (via localColabFold) to predict linear antibody epitopes, avoiding the need for labor-intensive empirical methods. The approach leverages recent advances in protein structure prediction to identify where antibodies bind to their antigens. This could streamline antibody research and development by providing a fast, cost-effective alternative to traditional epitope mapping.

papers.title: Spermidine attenuates monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension with HADHA-associated improvements in fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, impaired mitochondrial quality control, and mitochondrial redox imbalance are increasingly recognized as central drivers of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Spermidine (SPD) has been reported to exert cardiovascular protective effects; however, its effects on endothelial metabolism and redox homeostasis in PAH remain incompletely characterized. HADHA, the α-subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein, participates in long-chain fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) and provides a potential link between fatty acid utilization, mitochondrial respiration, mitophagy-relate
papers.summary: This study shows that spermidine supplementation reduces pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) severity in a monocrotaline rat model. The protective effect is linked to HADHA, a mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation enzyme, with improvements in fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial redox balance. The findings suggest spermidine may help correct metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction underlying PAH.

papers.title: Correction to "Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Tetrandrine Derivatives Targeting AKT1 for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Therapy: Integration of Network Pharmacology, Molecular Dynamics Simulation, and Experimental Validation".
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.5c13253.].
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on novel tetrandrine derivatives targeting AKT1 for hepatocellular carcinoma therapy. It does not present new data or findings, but rather corrects errors in the original paper. The correction likely addresses minor issues such as author affiliations, figures, or data reporting.

papers.title: Computational Design of RNA Aptamers Targeting Oncogenic miR-10b Using T‑SELEX and Molecular Dynamics-Based Stability Metrics.
papers.abstract: Aptamers are versatile single-stranded nucleic acids with high specificity and stability, making them ideal for targeting challenging biomolecules. Their structural flexibility enables selective recognition of nonprotein targets such as microRNAs (miRNAs). Among these, miR-10b plays a pivotal role in cancer progression and metastasis through its oncogenic 5p and 3p arms. We propose designing aptamers specifically targeting miR-10b through a computational framework to enable precise and efficient regulation of aberrant miRNA activity in cancer. Herein, we introduce a multiscale computational wo
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework for designing RNA aptamers that target the oncogenic microRNA miR-10b, combining a T-SELEX-based selection approach with molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate aptamer stability. The work aims to enable precise regulation of aberrant miRNA activity in cancer without relying on purely experimental screening.

papers.title: AlloPool is a deep learning framework that infers protein allostery from molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed protein structure prediction and design. However, protein function is governed not only by static structures but also by the conformational dynamics that allow proteins to access distinct functional states. Predicting these dynamic transitions, central to many biological processes, remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-resolution experimental data, which limits the training of machine-learning models for dynamic and energetic property prediction. Here, we present AlloPool, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that in
papers.summary: AlloPool is a graph neural network framework that learns to infer protein allostery—how binding at one site affects function at a distant site—directly from molecular dynamics simulation data. It addresses the scarcity of experimental dynamic data by training on simulations, enabling prediction of conformational transitions and energetic properties tied to allosteric regulation.

papers.title: Chemical Characterization and Pharmacological Activity of Byrsonima crassifolia (L.) Kunth (Murici): Antinociceptive Effects, Edema Reduction, and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the chemical composition, anti-inflammatory and antinociceptive activities of murici leaf (ELM) and bark (EBM) extracts using adult zebrafish (Danio rerio). HPLC analysis identified rutin, isoquercitrin, and kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside as the major phenolic compounds. Both extracts exhibited low toxicity and no sedative effects at the lowest tested doses. ELM showed abdominal antinociceptive activity mediated by TRPA1 and significantly reduced carrageenan-induced abdominal edema. EBM inhibited both corneal (TRPV1) and abdominal (TRPA1) nociception, producing effects simil
papers.summary: This study characterized the phenolic composition of murici (Byrsonima crassifolia) leaf and bark extracts, identifying rutin, isoquercitrin, and kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside as major compounds. Using zebrafish models, the extracts showed low toxicity and antinociceptive effects mediated by TRPA1 and TRPV1 channels, with the leaf extract also reducing carrageenan-induced edema. Molecular docking supported the interaction of these phenolics with the target ion channels.

papers.title: In Vitro Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Sour Cherry (Prunus cerasus L.) Seed Oil and Computational Safety Profiling.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the in vitro anti-inflammatory activity of sour cherry seed oils, including samples obtained by Soxhlet extraction and maceration, as well as ten commercial samples. The results demonstrated that the 15-lipoxygenase inhibitory activity of the oil samples ranged from 6% to 80%. Regarding cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition, while most samples showed negligible activity, the oil produced by Soxhlet extraction inhibited COX-1 and COX-2 by 38% and 32%, respectively. Similarly, the oil obtained via maceration showed inhibition rates of 25% and 23% for COX-1 and COX-2, respe
papers.summary: This study evaluated the anti-inflammatory activity of sour cherry seed oils from different extraction methods and commercial sources, finding that 15-lipoxygenase inhibition ranged widely from 6% to 80%, while COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition was generally weak except for Soxhlet-extracted oil (38% and 32%, respectively). Computational safety profiling was also performed to assess the oils' potential toxicity.

papers.title: Computational and Comparative In Vitro Evaluation of GC-MS Profiled Cannabis sativa Inflorescence Extracts' Metabolites on Selected Diabetes Therapeutic Targets.
papers.abstract: Cannabis sativa, a medicinal plant rich in cannabinoids, terpenoids, and flavonoids, has been shown to have various pharmacological activities. This study investigated the antidiabetic potential of C. sativa inflorescence extracts using in vitro and computational models. Dried C. sativa inflorescences were extracted sequentially with hexane, dichloromethane, and methanol, before their metabolites were identified by GC-MS. The extracts were tested for α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibition, glucose uptake activity, and antioxidant effects using DPPH and nitric oxide (NO) inhibition assays. Thir
papers.summary: This study profiled metabolites from Cannabis sativa inflorescence extracts using GC-MS and tested them for antidiabetic activity through in vitro enzyme inhibition assays (α-amylase, α-glucosidase), glucose uptake, and antioxidant assays, complemented by computational docking against diabetes-related targets. The extracts showed measurable antidiabetic and antioxidant potential, with specific cannabinoids, terpenoids, and flavonoids implicated as active compounds. The work is largely exploratory and preliminary, lacking in vivo validation.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Antimycobacterial Evaluation, and In Silico Investigation of Benzisothiazole-Based Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Tuberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A series of novel benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives was rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their antitubercular activity. Among the synthesized compounds, derivative 8k emerged as the most potent candidate, exhibiting a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.25 μg/mL, along with a high selectivity index (SI) of 42 and confirmed bactericidal activity. To gain preliminary insights into its possible mechanism of action, compound 8k was subjected to molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, using enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (InhA) as the
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives as potential anti-tuberculosis agents, with compound 8k showing potent activity (MIC 0.25 μg/mL) and a favorable selectivity index. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggest InhA as a possible target, providing a starting point for further optimization.

papers.title: Atomic-scale defect-mediated interfacial bonding in cold spray: FCC vs. BCC metal systems.
papers.abstract: The intense plastic deformation induced by the supersonic impact of powder particles during cold spray deposition determines particle-substrate interfacial properties. Herein, large-scale molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the atomistic microstructural evolution of similar particle-substrate systems during impact. The focus is placed on elucidating the distinct responses exhibited by a FCC metal system (such as Al-Al) versus a BCC metal system (such as Fe-Fe) to enable a systematic comparison of deformation mechanisms, defect generation, and phase transformations intrin
papers.summary: This study uses large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to compare how face-centered cubic (Al-Al) and body-centered cubic (Fe-Fe) metal systems evolve during cold spray impact. It reveals distinct deformation mechanisms, defect generation patterns, and phase transformations that govern atomic-scale interfacial bonding between particle and substrate.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum correcting a previously published computational study that screened Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors using molecular docking, ADMET, network pharmacology, molecular dynamics, and DFT. It contains no new scientific findings, only corrections to the original article.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and structural analysis to evaluate whether EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, can bind to the lysosomal enzyme GCase, which is deficient in Gaucher disease. The work aims to explore alternative molecular strategies for neuronopathic Gaucher disease, where current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies have limited brain impact. The findings are preliminary and based entirely on in silico modeling rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Computational insights into synergistic mechanisms of PD-901 and 5-azacitidine targeting PTPN11 (SHP2) E76K mutation in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
papers.abstract: Juvenile Myelomonocytic Leukemia (JMML) is an aggressive pediatric hematological cancer categorized by aberrant activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway. It is commonly caused by gain-of-function mutations, such as E76K in the PTPN11 protein. While 5-azacitidine (5-Aza) and the MEK inhibitor PD0325901 (PD-901) are not known direct inhibitors of SHP2/PTPN11, the reported activity of 5-Aza combined with MEK inhibition in PTPN11-mutated JMML offered a biological rationale for examining their potential structural interactions with SHP2.
papers.summary: This computational study investigates how the MEK inhibitor PD-901 and the hypomethylating agent 5-azacitidine might interact structurally with the mutant SHP2 (PTPN11 E76K) protein that drives juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia. Using molecular docking and dynamics simulations, the authors propose that these drugs could bind SHP2 directly, offering a mechanistic explanation for the clinical activity seen when they are combined. The work is purely in silico and suggests a potential new targeting strategy for a difficult pediatric cancer.

papers.title: Repurposed metformin-apigenin combination therapy for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: from integrative multi-omics discovery to in vivo validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease. Although recent drugs have been approved, the complex pathophysiology of MASH limits monotherapy efficacy and generates considerable inter-patient heterogeneity. The purpose of this research was to identify new molecular targets and develop a rational combination therapeutic approach for MASH.
papers.summary: This study used integrative multi-omics analysis to identify molecular targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and proposed a repurposed drug combination of metformin and apigenin. The combination was then validated in vivo, suggesting a rational polypharmacology strategy to address MASH heterogeneity.

papers.title: From drug export to envelope fitness: characterizing the regulatory landscape of selective Escherichia coli ABC efflux pumps.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance remains a top global health threat. While ATP-binding cassette (ABC) efflux pumps contribute to multidrug resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, their transcriptional regulation is far less understood than that of the RND and MFS families.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the transcriptional regulatory landscape of selective ABC efflux pumps in Escherichia coli, moving beyond their canonical role in drug export to examine how they contribute to envelope fitness. It addresses a gap in understanding compared to the better-studied RND and MFS efflux families, highlighting regulatory connections between efflux and membrane/ envelope stress responses.

papers.title: Integrated analysis of isorhamnetin-associated targets in chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer: immune-infiltration associations and antitumor effects in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) creates an inflammatory pancreatic microenvironment and is an established risk factor for pancreatic cancer (PC). However, immune-inflammatory links between CP and PC remain unclear. Isorhamnetin (ISO), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antitumor activities, may influence pancreatic inflammatory signaling. This study investigated ISO-associated molecular networks shared by CP and PC, examined the relationships between prioritized targets and transcriptome-estimated immune-cell infiltration, and evaluated the effects of ISO in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology and transcriptomic immune-infiltration analysis to identify isorhamnetin-associated molecular targets shared between chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer. The authors prioritize hub targets linked to immune cell infiltration and validate isorhamnetin's antitumor effects in pancreatic cancer cell lines. The work suggests isorhamnetin may modulate the inflammatory-immune axis connecting CP to PC progression.

papers.title: Targeting cancer hallmarks with microbiome-derived bacteriocins and postbiotics: molecular mechanisms and translational opportunities in oncology.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome is an abundant reservoir of bioactive molecules with considerable therapeutic potential in oncology. Among these microbial products, bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites have emerged as promising anticancer agents due to their diverse biological activities and ability to modulate multiple cancer-related pathways. Growing evidence suggests that microbiome-derived compounds may provide novel opportunities for the development of safer and more targeted cancer therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review examines how bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites produced by the human microbiome can act as anticancer agents by targeting multiple hallmarks of cancer. It discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects and outlines translational opportunities for developing safer, more targeted cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis prioritizes compartment-specific candidate targets of gut microbiota metabolites in diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: The gut-kidney axis has emerged as a critical area of investigation. However, the compartment-specific regulatory mechanisms of gut microbiota metabolites within the glomerular and tubulointerstitial regions of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify compartment-specific candidate targets through which gut microbiota metabolites may influence diabetic kidney disease, distinguishing effects in glomerular versus tubulointerstitial regions. It highlights the gut-kidney axis as a regulatory mechanism and prioritizes potential targets for further investigation. The work is primarily hypothesis-generating, providing candidate targets rather than validated mechanisms.
